proof.criterion: The reviewer's two prose claims about the code are true: an unset streamMaxBytes sets no limit rather than a binary default, and the plugin decodes the three settings so an undecodable value refuses the Construct (review.json, minor findings 2 and 4).
proof.surface: The bus package's own source for the first, and the plugin's Construct path — the released component's decoding — for the second, driven through pulumitest.Construct.
proof.command: read packages/envoy/internal/bus/nats.go:136-151 and :163-173; and a throwaway probe file (gcp/zz_tester_probe2_test.go, deleted before this handoff) run with `go test ./gcp/ -run TestProbeConstruct -v`
proof.observed: bus.ParseStreamMaxBytes's own doc comment reads `unset or blank is 0, which sets no limit (a deployed stream keeps the one it has)`, which is now what dispatch.go, the README and the test comment say, word for word; the old wording (`each binary keeps its own default`) was wrong, so the reviewer's fix is right. On the Construct path, `natsInCluster` given as the string "yes" is refused with `copying input "natsInCluster": unmarshaling value: expected a bool, got a string`, and `natsReplicas` given as 2.5 with `envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch example-dispatch: natsReplicas 2.5 must be a whole number`. Beyond the comment's claim: through that same Construct path both containers render ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS=3, ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES=67108864 and no ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY key, so the plugin carries the three settings all the way into the rendering, which is the gap the code-quality pass raised and no committed test asserts.
proof.negativeControl: An input name the resource does not have (`natsInClusterTypo`) is accepted silently rather than refused — the Pulumi provider SDK ignores an extra key, which is not what the comment claims and is no change of this pull request. Recorded so that the comment is not read as a guarantee against a misspelt input name.

observations.what: O1 (round 1, unchanged and still open as a scheduling rule, not a defect): natsInCluster and natsUrl must change in one apply. With natsInCluster set and a natsUrl naming the hub's tailnet MagicDNS name — what production carries today — the component renders with no proxy at all and neither NATS client can resolve its hub.
observations.evidence: Measured from this worker pod, an ordinary cluster pod with no tailscale sidecar: `getent hosts` of the hub's tailnet name exits 2 and resolves nothing, while `getent hosts envoy-hub.envoy.svc.cluster.local` answers the ClusterIP of Service envoy-hub in namespace envoy. Production's two NATS clients each run in a pod of one container with no tailscale sidecar, so the tailnet name works for them today only through ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY and the front-door pod, which is a tailnet node. This round adds one more sighting: dispatchConstructInputs() itself sets natsInCluster true beside a tailnet natsUrl and the component accepts it without a word, which is exactly the shape an operator would produce by flipping one input.
observations.judgement: Settled by INFRA-14's architect on 2026-10-29: the code stays as it is, and INFRA-553's spec version 23 carries both the one-apply rule (with natsUrl set to the in-cluster Service name) and the ordering rule below. Nothing for this pull request.

observations.what: O2 (round 1, unchanged): applying natsInCluster before INFRA-551's bridge policy admits namespace dispatch fails asymmetrically — the app rolls fully and serves with no bus, while the listener's rollout stalls.
observations.evidence: envoy-dispatch's readiness reads only Postgres and reports nats false meanwhile; envoy-listener exits on a failed initial connect (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go). Both Deployments roll with maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1, so the listener's rollout holds its old pods while the app's completes.
observations.judgement: Settled in INFRA-553 spec version 23: the apply runs only after INFRA-551's policy is applied, and reads both rollouts complete and the app's /healthz reporting NATS connected.
